title: First playable prototype vs the build I'm launching. What changed once I brought AI art in
author: NicoBacc
selftext:
Left side of the video is the very first playable version of Vaelix: coloured circles on a dark grid, a list of heroes and a "Lock plan" button. Right side is what I'm launching on November 1st. It took me about a year to get from one to the other, working on it next to my normal job.



Some context on me. I've been building mobile apps and websites for about 10 years, and a few years back I made a multiplayer racing game in Unity on my own. Programmer art, and it showed. So this time I made the call early: the game logic is mine, the visuals come from AI image tools, because I'm just not a designer.



The thing nobody tells you is that the art is not one problem, it's three. Getting a nice hero portrait is easy. Getting the same hero to still look like the same hero as a tiny sprite on the board is harder. And the arenas were the worst part. This month I moved the board to a tilted camera, so each arena is one big generated image and the game projects the 6x8 grid onto its floor. The model never put the floor exactly where I asked, so I ended up measuring the four corners of the floor on every image by hand.



Everything that moves on the arenas (torches, lava, waterfalls, flags) is done in code on top of the static image, not generated as animation. Way lighter on the phone and it never flickers between frames.



The game itself: 3 heroes vs 3, both players plan at the same time and then the round resolves all at once. Out November 1st on Android and iOS, links on vaelix.app.

This is the website if you want to stay updated with the launch: [Vaelix](https://vaelix.app)
